meta.title: Suntiq security and backend review
meta.description: Production verdict, corrected security findings, trust-boundary map, merge proof, plan alignment, and the shortest safe remediation path.

props.title: Keep the merge. Do not promote it yet.
props.subtitle: The branch is strictly better than both parents, but one life-safety flaw and two identity/deployment gates still block production.

props.label: Current ruling
props.title: Three decisions, no ambiguity
props.subtitle: Merge quality, production safety, and architecture are separate claims.

props.title: Keep b627 and the upstream merge
props.content: The merge preserves the incoming backend/security work, closes two timestamp and engine-alert defects, and replaces starvation with a bounded latency trade. Reverting any part would reintroduce a verified safety defect.
props.next: Land the blocker fixes on top of this state.

props.title: Production promotion
props.content: A future caller-supplied man-overboard timestamp can silently suppress a genuine alert. Device attribution and production credential configuration also need proof before the relevant ingest lane is trusted.
props.next: Close C-1, prove device containment or identity, and verify required production envs.

props.title: Keep the modular monolith
props.content: One Convex deployment with explicit trust choke points is the correct shape. The failures are missing guards inside existing boundaries, not evidence for microservices or per-tenant infrastructure.
props.next: Harden the four trust planes locally; introduce cells only when a contract forces them.

props.label: Security architecture
props.title: Four trust planes, three promotion gates
props.subtitle: Every blocker sits at an existing choke point. The topology does not need to change.

props.title: The silent-failure multiplier
props.content: C-1 is the decisive blocker because it suppresses the safety event and all downstream routing while remaining invisible to the victim organization. H-5 and the environment gate determine whether telemetry can be attributed to a real device rather than merely a reachable network source.

props.label: Finding ledger
props.title: All findings, with final severity and disposition
props.subtitle: This table reconciles the Opus review with the independent architecture pass. Severity follows exploitability, exposure, and silent-failure cost.

rows.finding: Caller-controlled future `at` plus org-blind dedup can suppress a real MOB alert and every delivery channel.
rows.exposure: Reachable by a self-service org against an unstamped boat code; silent for the victim org.
rows.fix: Clamp to server time, require `createdAt <= at`, and scope dedup to the owning org.

rows.finding: The legacy boat server injects its ingest token into every rendered HTML page.
rows.exposure: Blocks public or untrusted exposure of the legacy boat server; deferred if that lane is not deployed.
rows.fix: Remove the token from `htmlInject()` and prove `GET /` contains no secret.

rows.finding: `POST /api/ai` is an unauthenticated provider-backed LLM proxy.
rows.exposure: High when the legacy boat server is network-reachable and provider credentials are enabled.
rows.fix: Apply the existing `authorized(req)` guard before provider work.

rows.finding: `X-Forwarded-For` is trusted unconditionally, so a caller can evade IP rate buckets.
rows.exposure: Medium alone; a high-impact amplifier for H-2.
rows.fix: Honor forwarded addresses only when an explicit trusted-proxy mode is enabled.

rows.finding: `ai.narrate` accepts unbounded prompt/system input and its fallback request is not separately charged.
rows.exposure: Authenticated and metered through `requireOrgMember`; this is bounded cost/control weakness, not anonymous access.
rows.fix: Reuse `truncateTail` limits and charge the fallback provider round.

rows.finding: Droplet attribution maps source IP, port, or CIDR to a boat, then signs frames with that boat credential.
rows.exposure: Production-blocking unless private APN or VPN containment is proven; shared carrier CIDRs are not device identity.
rows.fix: Prefer a frame-level device secret. At minimum prove the listener is unreachable outside the contained network.

rows.finding: `push.removeToken` deletes matching push rows without an authenticated principal.
rows.exposure: Requires learning a high-entropy Expo token; push remains one additive channel.
rows.fix: Require the user and scope deletion to that user's token rows.

rows.finding: `setArmState` omits `codeVisibleToOrg`, allowing cross-org state on unresolved same-code boats.
rows.exposure: Tenant-integrity problem on unstamped telemetry; stamped foreign telemetry is filtered.
rows.fix: Apply the same ownership helper already used by the safety-alert sibling.

rows.finding: The rotating link watchdog caps rows examined, including healthy rows, so stale detection latency scales with fleet size.
rows.exposure: Operability and delayed relay-silent detection; b627 still improves the prior starvation failure.
rows.fix: Rotate through the ring but stop after the cap of stale rows processed, not rows examined.

rows.finding: Webhook delivery validates the registered host but follows redirects without validating each hop.
rows.exposure: Admin-gated blind SSRF toward internal or metadata destinations.
rows.fix: Use `redirect: manual` and re-run the existing sink-host check per hop.

rows.finding: Telemetry history has no server-owned `source`, no `ingestId`, no receipt table, and time-only pruning.
rows.exposure: Permanent provenance and custody gap against ADR-008; not directly attacker-reachable.
rows.fix: Stamp `source` and `ingestId` at ingest first; add decoded receipts before prune second.

rows.finding: Public REST endpoints have no rate limit, while every valid call patches one `lastUsedAt` document.
rows.exposure: Leaked-key abuse and write contention under load.
rows.fix: Rate by key ID and coarsen `lastUsedAt` updates.

rows.finding: At-least-once ingest unconditionally inserts duplicate position breadcrumbs.
rows.exposure: Replays inflate distance and any breadcrumb-derived aggregate.
rows.fix: Use the ADR-008 `ingestId` as the idempotency key.

rows.finding: The AI tools security comment claims verified org injection, but the caller supplies the org ID.
rows.exposure: No current cross-tenant hole: all six downstream queries call `requireOrg` first.
rows.fix: Correct the comment and mechanically guard the six-executor invariant.

rows.finding: `reportDtuLink` skips the auto-registration cap.
rows.exposure: Unbounded `dtuLinks` storage growth; cost rather than compromise.

rows.finding: Responses do not set CSP, HSTS, or frame-ancestors.
rows.exposure: Defense in depth; no matching XSS sink was found.
rows.source: Legacy boat server and web response headers
rows.fix: Add headers when the deployment surface and embed contract are settled.

footer.finding: Severity is reconciled, not copied from the first reviewer.

props.label: Reviewer reconciliation
props.title: What changed after architecture review
props.subtitle: The second pass kept the defects but corrected four severities and narrowed the deployment claims.

rows.finding: H-3 proxy trust
rows.why: Rate-limit bypass is an amplifier; the unauthenticated AI route carries the high impact.

rows.finding: H-4 ai.narrate
rows.why: The route is authenticated and metered through `requireOrgMember`; the real defect is uncapped inputs plus fallback accounting.

rows.finding: H-6 remove push token
rows.why: Destructive and unauthenticated, but exploitation needs a high-entropy token and push is additive.

rows.finding: H-7 arm state
rows.why: A real tenant-integrity issue concentrated in unresolved same-code telemetry, not a universal cross-tenant path.

props.title: Deployment evidence still missing
props.content: `SUNTIQ_FLEET_DEVICE_TOKEN`, `DEVICE_CREDENTIAL_PEPPER`, and `API_KEY_PEPPER` must be proven present in production without displaying their values. The code intentionally accepts never-credentialed boats when the fleet token is unset, so a green source review cannot substitute for environment proof.

props.label: Safety correction
props.title: The three b627 changes
props.subtitle: Two are correct fixes. One is a sound starvation fix with a measurable latency trade.

props.label: Correct
props.title: Future telemetry timestamps clamp at the choke point
props.content: Every high-water writer now derives from server-bounded time. A year-2200 telemetry report can no longer advance prune cutoffs and erase retained history.

props.label: Correct
props.title: Overheat hysteresis now fires and re-fires correctly
props.content: The hard-threshold previous-state check and acknowledged-open duplicate behavior are coupled. Removing either hunk reintroduces a failure.

props.label: Keep, then tune
props.title: Rotation removes starvation but delays sparse stale detection
props.content: The ring rotation is mathematically sound. The window now counts healthy rows examined, so detection latency grows with fleet size. Fix the accounting, not the rotation.

props.label: Architecture plan
props.title: What is implemented, partial, missing, or outside this review
props.subtitle: The largest remaining gap is data provenance and custody, not service decomposition.

rows.next: Add structural accessor and CI guard so future code cannot bypass it.

rows.evidence: Single deployment with server-side platform-admin checks.
rows.next: Keep one deployment until a contract forces dedicated cells.

rows.evidence: Implemented in `dtu-ingest`, outside the reviewed ArgoEdge tree.
rows.next: Verify bucket, IAM, capture, and receipt behavior in the owning repo.

rows.evidence: Insert-only history path and monotonic guards exist.
rows.next: Add server-owned provenance, idempotency, and custody receipts.

Add one server-owned ID and enforce uniqueness where history is inserted.
Require a decoded archive receipt naming the exact rows to delete.

rows.evidence: No provenance field exists to quarantine or filter.
rows.next: Add the source contract before evidence readers depend on it.

rows.evidence: Minted or revoked credentials fail closed.

rows.next: Keep model output subordinate to deterministic authorization.

The audit still lists b627-fixed criticals as open; ADR numbering also collides.

props.label: Controls that held
props.title: The review also tried to break the controls that matter
props.subtitle: These are not assumptions; each survived a targeted source or counterexample check.

props.title: Tenant authorization
props.content: `requireOrg` verifies membership on the passed org ID. All six AI tool queries call it before reading data.

props.title: Credential revocation
props.content: Once a boat has minted credentials, a fully revoked credential does not fall back to anonymous access.

props.title: History mass-deletion vector
props.content: The future telemetry timestamp counterexample fails because prune derives from the clamped server-bounded time.

props.title: REST tenant scope
props.content: The API key determines the organization. Public endpoints do not accept a caller-supplied org ID.

props.title: Stripe verification
props.content: Raw body, constant-time HMAC, replay window, and no side effects before verification all hold.

props.title: Naming and compatibility
props.content: User-facing identity is `Suntiq`; the AI persona is `Sofia`. Technical compatibility identifiers remain intentionally stable.

props.label: Regression contract
props.title: Five checks that keep this fixed
props.subtitle: Each is the smallest executable claim that would fail if the boundary regresses.

rows.invariant: No alert row stores `createdAt` later than server now.
A future unacked row cannot suppress a genuine same-type alert.
rows.proves: C-1 dedup lower and upper bounds.

rows.invariant: Every exported mutation reaches a user, org, or device principal.
No boat-server HTTP response contains an ingest secret.
One stale link alerts within two sweeps; every AI tool query starts with `requireOrg`.
rows.proves: M-1 liveness and the L-1 tenant invariant.

props.label: Next move
props.title: The shortest safe sequence
props.subtitle: Do not mix enterprise maturity work into the promotion blockers.

items.title: Close C-1 at the shared alert boundary
items.description: Clamp caller time, bound dedup, scope it to the owning org, and add the unstamped same-code counterexample.

items.title: Prove device identity and production secrets
items.description: Verify token and pepper presence without revealing values. Prove private network containment or ship frame-level device identity.

items.title: Harden any exposed legacy boat server
items.description: Only if deployed: remove the HTML secret, authenticate the AI route, and trust forwarded addresses only behind an explicit proxy contract.

items.title: Land bounded medium corrections
items.description: H-4, H-6, H-7, M-1, M-2, and M-4 are local changes with focused checks.

items.title: Implement ADR-008 provenance and custody
items.description: Source and ingestId first; receipt-gated pruning and evidence-reader policy second.

props.title: Avoid the architecture detour
props.content: Do not split services, add per-tenant deployments, or introduce a second authorization framework. The first four gates are existing-helper changes at existing choke points. Dedicated cells remain a contract-triggered future option.
